title: Canonical coefficient comparisons preserve inverse-image square transport
statement: Let Λ and Λ′ be commutative rings in Type(u+1), φ:Λ→Λ′ a ring homomorphism, and let e:Y→T, h:Y→X, g:T→S, p:X→S satisfy e≫g=h≫p. Let U_f be the canonical bounded below inverse-image coefficient comparison of [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons], and θ:h^*p^*≅e^*g^* the inverse-image square comparison appearing in [sbc-def-base-change-map]. For every L in D⁺(S_et,Λ′), the composite h^*(U_p(L)), then U_h(p′^*L), then Res_Y(θ′(L)), equals θ(Res_S L), then e^*(U_g(L)), then U_e(g′^*L). This is only an identity between composite inverse images; it uses neither derived direct image nor adjunction unit or counit. No cartesian hypothesis beyond commutativity is required.

proof.text: For each pair of composable scheme morphisms, the inverse-image composition isomorphism identifies the composite adjunction with the adjunction for the composite morphism. Direct image and coefficient coextension commute sectionwise. Uniqueness of left adjoints is transitive and respects composite adjunctions, so the canonical coefficient comparison respects inverse-image composition.

Apply the preceding composition identity to h followed by p and to e followed by g. The equality h≫p=e≫g identifies the composite functors and their coefficient comparisons. Cancel the composition isomorphism on one side to obtain the square identity. Exact derivation preserves this equality and its composition isomorphisms are natural, giving the stated D⁺ equation.
